Table 2 prints Lubunga (Tshopo) with 1 cumulative case and 0 deaths and no harmonisation footnote, as in SR186, after SR185 printed 2 deaths marked as being harmonised. The Tshopo row moves from 33 deaths in SR186 to 35 by exactly its 2 deaths of the day. The zone values are kept as printed.

Nord-Kivu care prints 577 patients (118 confirmed, 459 suspects; 314 in CTE/CT on 434 beds and 263 in health facilities outside CTE/CT) after 107 admissions and 80 exits (1 recovered, 70 non-cases, 9 deaths) and prints no carry-over. SR186 printed 521 patients (312 in CTE/CT and 209 outside) at the end of its day; 521 + 107 - 80 = 548, not 577. With no carry-over printed in SR187, the figures of the edition itself close (118 + 459 = 577 and 314 + 263 = 577), so the census, its split and the CTE/CT and outside counts are kept as printed and the non-closure against SR186 is recorded here. The printed occupancy of 72% is stated as 314 of 434 beds and is kept only as the printed rate. The exits count 9 deaths without a status split; Table 2 prints 6 intra-CTE confirmed deaths for Nord-Kivu.

Ituri care prints 397 patients (151 confirmed, 246 suspects) after 84 admissions and 77 exits and prints no carry-over; SR186 printed 394 at the end of its day, and 394 + 84 - 77 = 401, not 397. With no carry-over printed in SR187 and a split that closes (151 + 246 = 397), the census and split are kept as printed and the non-closure against SR186 is recorded here; the printed occupancy of 37% (27% confirmed, 48% suspects) is kept only as the printed rate. The exits count 16 deaths of which 11 confirmed, while Table 2 prints 5 intra-CTE confirmed deaths for Ituri. Hot meals for 362 of 379 patients use a denominator that differs from the census; both are kept as printed.

Tshopo care prints 17 patients carried over (6 confirmed, 11 suspects), the same total as the SR186 end of day (5 confirmed and 12 suspects), 2 admissions and 5 exits (4 non-cases and 1 death), then 12 patients (4 confirmed, 8 suspects); 17 + 2 - 5 = 14, not 12. The printed occupancy of 30% is stated as 12 of 40 beds, while the two sites print 32 and 4 beds (36). The census, split and occupancy are withheld; admissions and exits are kept as printed.

Haut-Uele care prints 73 patients (38 confirmed, 35 suspects), which follows from the SR186 printed census (65 = 36 confirmed + 29 suspects): 65 + 15 admissions - 5 exits - 2 deaths = 73, and the split closes exactly from the SR186 printed split of 36 confirmed and 29 suspects (36 + 4 - 2 = 38 confirmed; 29 + 11 - 5 = 35 suspects; 73), the 2 deaths matching the 2 intra-CTE confirmed deaths in Table 2. It prints an occupancy of 40% with 42% for confirmed and 38% for suspects. SR185 printed the same three rates for 65 patients (29 confirmed, 36 suspects) and SR186 printed 40% for 65 patients; the rates repeat while the census changes and are withheld. The 4 confirmed admissions compare with 2 new Haut-Uele cases in Table 1.

Bas-Uele care prints 24 suspects carried over, against 25 at the end of SR186, then 20 admissions and 2 non-case exits for 42 suspects in isolation (24 + 20 - 2 = 42); the nutrition and SMSPS lines of the same edition print 43 suspects. The census is withheld because the edition prints it both as 42 and as 43; the carry-over difference against SR186 (24 against 25) is recorded only. The admissions and exits are kept as printed.

Nord-Ubangi care prints 28 patients of whom 13 confirmed in isolation, while the same paragraph prints 8 confirmed patients admitted to the CTE since the start (3 recovered, 1 died) and Table 1 prints 10 cumulative Nord-Ubangi cases; it prints hot meals for 32 patients and an occupancy of 160% or 90% depending on the indicator. Vaccination lines carry internal conflicts: Nord-Kivu prints 1 non-serious adverse event as 0.018 per 1 000 (1 of 3 901 vaccinated is 0.26 per 1 000; 0.018 is 1 of 5 500 doses as a percentage); Ituri prints a cumulative 443 vaccinated made of 199 women and 254 men (453), after SR186 printed a cumulative 4 326. The Nord-Kivu cumulative (3 637 in SR186 + 264 = 3 901) and the dose balance (3 901 used + 1 598 left + 1 lost = 5 500) reconcile. Vaccination counts are not promoted.

Lines that restate earlier editions are not promoted as new SR187 events: the Bas-Uele PCI assessment (130 of 632 providers trained, 16 of 20 and 17 of 20 facilities without triage or water), the Nord-Ubangi PCI challenges, the Haut-Uele SMSPS counts (identical to SR186) and the Nord-Kivu SMSPS stock lines (112, 163, 251, 123 households, 63 PPL, 33/33 and 471 in psychoeducation, as in SR186; its new-case line, 31/36 against 20/30, and its 138 result announcements with 36 positive, against 121 with 30, are new and not promoted because SMSPS counts are not carried), the Bas-Uele security challenges (worded as in the SR184 and SR185 security lines), the Ituri strike line (since SR185) and the 7 of 43 Ituri ambulances out of service (as in SR185 and SR186).

A logistics line labelled Haut-Uele reports stockouts in 4 of 6 reporting CTE at sites in an Ituri health zone and a vaccine pre-stockout alert in Ituri; the province attribution is unclear and the line is not promoted.
Single-patient details in the PoE/PoC, care, laboratory, logistics and security paragraphs (ages, case numbers, named control points, facilities and burial sites) are not carried.

challenges.finding: Publisher reports, in Nord-Kivu, security blockages hindering PCI work, no household given a kit (3 of 24 decontaminated), a low facility score card average (47.4%, none at 80%), 8 of 23 exposed staff at high risk and swab failures for lack of PCI inputs (no count promoted); in Ituri team shortages (Mangala, Mandima), PCI input stockouts (Mandima, Nyankunde, Mambasa), saturation in several care facilities, 17 patients without hot meals in Mandima and burials deferred because of operational shortfalls in Mandima and Bunia; in Haut-Uele community resistance that stopped ring opening in Isiro and a community refusal of a safe burial; in Tshopo swab failures and a need for training of mortuary agents (no count promoted), insecurity and supply difficulties for specialty products; in Bas-Uele a provider strike and no nutritional support for isolated suspects; and hand-washing refusals at control points (5 943 in Ituri, 2 018 in Nord-Kivu, 372 in Haut-Uele and 304 in Tshopo) linked to rumours. Lines restating earlier editions (Bas-Uele PCI assessment, Nord-Ubangi PCI challenges, Bas-Uele security challenges, the Ituri strike and ambulance lines) are not counted here. No intervention effect is established.
